proposals.name: UCSF Medical Education: Opportunities for High School Students (HealthLink)
proposals.why: UCSF's page of high-school health-career programs. HealthLink is a free year-long mentoring program with monthly Saturday sessions, October 2026 to May 2027, and prefers sophomores.
proposals.eligibility_note: Strict limits: students must be first-generation college-bound, meet disadvantaged or low-income criteria, and be referred by a partner group or teacher. Ridhi probably doesn't qualify. It's worth tracking only because the page may add other UCSF high-school programs.

proposals.name: Playing At Learning / NorCalFLL — FIRST LEGO League & FTC event list (Northern California)
proposals.why: Playing At Learning runs all FIRST robotics programs for Northern California and this page publishes every dated qualifier — including ones at Dorris-Eaton in San Ramon and BASIS Dublin.
proposals.eligibility_note: FLL Challenge is grades 4-8 (ages 9-14) in teams up to 10 — exactly Dhruv's bracket; FLL Explore is K-4 and FIRST Tech Challenge is grades 7-12, so the same page keeps working as he ages up. Competing requires joining a registered team; the 2026-27 BIOGLOW tournament-preference window already closed

proposals.name: City of San Ramon — Open Gym (badminton at Iron Horse Gymnasium)
proposals.why: Lowest-friction local badminton: drop-in city sessions a few minutes from home, no academy enrollment or season commitment.
proposals.eligibility_note: Page does not state a minimum age or any youth/teen rule, and badminton day/time is not in the page text (prices appear only inside an image) — confirm whether an 11-year-old may play and whether an adult must accompany him before relying on it. Paid per-entry or multi-entry pass.

proposals.name: Bay Badminton Training Academy — academy classes and monthly schedule
proposals.why: Nonprofit youth badminton academy with a graded ladder (Beginner through Elite) and a monthly schedule PDF, i.e. a real coaching pathway rather than drop-in play.
proposals.eligibility_note: Class descriptions list Beginner / Intermediate / Advanced as ages 6-19 (Dhruv fits), 'High School' as 13-19, and a Special Class at 8-19. LOCATION IS UNVERIFIED: a third-party nonprofit directory lists a Dublin CA address, but the academy's own site states no city and points to a partner facility (

proposals.name: Acton Children's Business Fair — young-entrepreneur marketplace network
proposals.why: A one-day real market where a kid builds a product, prices it and sells it — the most hands-on version of Dhruv's finance/business interest, and age-appropriate in a way most entrepreneurship programs are not.
proposals.eligibility_note: Ages 6-17, so Dhruv is squarely eligible. Fairs are city-hosted: the national site links only San Francisco and Los Angeles for California, and the Bay Area fairs that surfaced in search (Concord, and Dublin at Emerald Glen Park) came from third-party calendars with conflicting dates and nothing con

proposals.name: Washington Health (Washington Hospital, Fremont) — High School Volunteer Program
proposals.why: An actual in-hospital teen volunteer pipeline in the East Bay that is not yet on the list, and the page publishes concrete waitlist open/close dates worth diffing.
proposals.eligibility_note: 16+ with age verification — Ridhi is 15, so this is a WATCHLIST item, not an apply-now. Seniors are told not to apply (long onboarding). Process is join-the-waitlist by email, then invitation to a Prospective Volunteer Information Session as hospital need allows; the page states the high-school wait

proposals.name: Stanford Splash (Stanford ESP) — weekend of student-taught classes, held fall and spring
proposals.why: Twice a year, Stanford students teach short classes on many subjects, including biology and medicine; the homepage banner announces each date.
proposals.eligibility_note: Grades 8-12, so Ridhi is eligible now and Dhruv will be in 8th grade. Spots are given by lottery (Phase 0).

proposals.name: Berkeley Math Tournament — BMT (high school) and BmMT (middle school)
proposals.why: Student-run UC Berkeley math competitions for teams or solo entrants. BmMT is for middle schoolers, and BMT allows advanced younger students.
proposals.eligibility_note: BmMT is for grade 8 or below, so it fits Dhruv; in 2026 it ran in April and online in June. BMT is for grade 12 or below with no minimum age.

proposals.name: NSDA Springboard Series — free online speech & debate scrimmages
proposals.why: Free online scrimmages roughly weekly, with a 'rising stars' division for middle schoolers and first-year competitors; a low-stakes way for Dhruv to start debating.
proposals.eligibility_note: Middle schoolers can enter. Students cannot sign up on their own: they must enter under their school, with a coach registering them through Tabroom, so Pine Valley needs a sponsoring teacher or coach.

proposals.name: Skyline College — Science in Action seminar series
proposals.why: Free science talks from working biomedical, biotech and drug-discovery scientists, with a Zoom option.
proposals.eligibility_note: Free and open to the public. The page lists no age restriction, and it is aimed at college students. The campus is in San Bruno, so Zoom is the practical way to attend.

proposals.name: Vitalant — volunteer portal (regional shift listings)
proposals.why: Open shifts for the Vitalant blood-drive and donor-lounge volunteer roles, searchable by ZIP code.
proposals.eligibility_note: No minimum age is stated on the Vitalant volunteer page. Confirm it before applying, since blood-drive roles often require 16+. I did not fetch the portal itself, so the URL comes from the Vitalant volunteer page and is unconfirmed.
